contract: Store-only PostgreSQL translation using a consumer-owned Ecto Repo and optional prefix: atomic append CAS, immutable records/checkpoints, outbox ack and bounded retention. Migration helper only; no shipped Repo/config/Application.
limits: Subset only: no general SQL API, CDC, SQLite, migration framework, database-per-service, replication or disk/fsync guarantee.
Atomic append capability; torn-tail repair always rejected: torn_repair_unsupported, or caller_transaction inside the caller's open Ecto transaction.

Calls inside the caller's open Ecto transaction on the same Repo are refused before any statement: writes return {:rejected, :caller_transaction}, reads {:error, :caller_transaction} (ELZ-032 bug fix, same ID). Transactions opened outside Ecto on the same connection are not detected.
The caller-transaction check is per process: Repo.in_transaction?/0 sees only the calling process's checked-out connection.

Under Ecto.Adapters.SQL.Sandbox in_transaction? is false: the Store's transaction becomes a savepoint, a write can return {:committed, n} after only RELEASE SAVEPOINT and the sandbox rollback erases it, so the refusal does not apply. Consumer test suites using the Sandbox must not treat committed as a real COMMIT.
A raw BEGIN inside Repo.checkout/2 is not detected; writes then return indeterminate(:unavailable) and reads :unavailable.
Calls from another process, including every Writer call, are never refused; they commit on their own connection independently of the caller's transaction, so there is no transaction-scoped atomicity.

Static, I/O-free validation runs before the caller-transaction check, so invalid input inside a caller transaction keeps its existing rejection or indeterminate(:malformed_reply) result; no SQL is issued in either case.
PostgreSQL transaction/locking/storage behavior is upstream; finite local tests do not establish universal durability or exactly-once effects.
Consumers own the Repo, schema deployment, access control, fsync/synchronous_commit, backups and operational recovery.

grounding.claim: K1–K11 plus D11/D15/D17/D19 on a disposable PostgreSQL database: restart, late commits, backend termination, unavailable service, corruption, FK and lock ordering; ELZ-032 caller-transaction refusal for every write callback and every read callback except the static capabilities, with outer COMMIT and ROLLBACK, the outer transaction still usable, and the shell results through Outbox/Checkpoint/confirm. Missing/unreachable URL fails closed.
Local step-4 test observation: PostgreSQL 14.24, fsync=on, synchronous_commit=on. Test prints actual settings; not a production or all-execution claim.
Ecto SQL 3.14.0 transaction, SQL and consumer Repo integration are upstream contracts, including nested Repo.transaction joining the caller's transaction and the process-local Repo.in_transaction?/0.
Postgrex 0.22.4 protocol, connection and error behavior are upstream contracts.
PostgreSQL transaction atomicity, uniqueness, row locking, WAL/fsync and crash semantics are upstream server contracts reached through Postgrex, not local proofs.
Elixir validation, exceptions and BEAM execution are upstream contracts, not proved here.
OTP 29.1.2 GenServer, process lifecycle and crypto APIs are upstream contracts; no disk durability or exactly-once guarantee.

The consumer configures an appropriate PostgreSQL service (including fsync/synchronous_commit), schema permissions and maintenance; tests exercise named local scenarios, not the consumer's production deployment.

telemetry.contract: Consumer Ecto Repo emits upstream events; Elzoo adds no telemetry events.

config.contract: Consumer Repo module and optional SQL prefix; no global Repo/config shipped.

control.contract: Consumer owns Repo lifecycle; no separate Elzoo database control process.
